content: 1. A technical working group, composed of experts in Human Resources for Health (HRH) data, may be established as a sub-group within a larger multi-stakeholder group. This group can be tasked with specific technical activities, which may be supported by external expertise when necessary. Examples of such activities include conducting a scoping analysis of the current HRH data situation in the country, providing guidance on selecting data sources, identifying data gaps and organizing multiple sources to address these gaps, and drafting summary reports on analyzed data for validation by the multi-stakeholder working group. 2. A communications team, nominated by the multi-stakeholder working group, is responsible for ensuring a coherent, widespread, and consistent communication strategy to disseminate and publish results from the National Health Workforce Accounts (NHWA) in relevant media. This team also assists the technical working group in publishing NHWA results in scientific journals. Participants in these groups may have overlapping roles, and the focal point from the Ministry of Health could play a valuable role across all groups. 3. The first step in implementing NHWA is to secure governmental buy-in. This involves obtaining political commitment to strengthen HRH data, ensuring the Ministry of Health adopts the NHWA framework, and taking initial steps to coordinate an intersectoral health workforce agenda. Tasks include identifying a health workforce representative within the Ministry of Health to act as the NHWA focal point, consolidating available resources for NHWA, preparing a brief to highlight the need for NHWA, identifying existing information systems relevant to NHWA, and preparing documents required for Ministry of Health approval. The main outputs include the Ministry of Health taking leadership to strengthen HRH data and initiating implementation with a multi-year plan. 4. Establishing governance for NHWA involves creating a governance structure with representatives from relevant sectors and stakeholders. Tasks include stakeholder mapping by the Ministry of Health focal point, nominating a focal point from each stakeholder, setting up a multi-sector, multi-stakeholder coordination working group with defined governance and coordination mechanisms, nominating a secretariat to centralize data and organize documentation, and nominating a technical working group to handle data gathering and analysis. The main outputs include the establishment of a multi-sector, multi-stakeholder coordination working group, defined governance and coordination mechanisms, adoption of key policy questions, establishment of a secretariat, and creation of a communications structure. 5. The scoping and planning phase aims to produce evidence of the state of HRH in the country as a foundation for NHWA, develop a national and global dissemination plan, and define the business plan for NHWA implementation, including securing catalytic funding for the initial phase. Tasks include complementing the technical working group with external experts if necessary, conducting a scoping analysis, reviewing NHWA indicators, performing a maturity model assessment on the NHWA online platform, preparing a data analysis and dissemination plan, and holding a meeting to cost the first year and plan a rolling budget. The main outputs include a completed scoping analysis, preparation of the first-year costing and rolling budget plan, and development of an analysis plan. 6. The legal framework phase involves assessing the national legal environment for governance of the multi-stakeholder working group, data protection rules, and regulations. It also includes obtaining legal authorization for data extraction, exchange, and dissemination, and ensuring legal requirements are shared and standard operating procedures (SOPs) are adopted. Tasks include identifying relevant national bodies for ethics, data confidentiality, anonymization, and data exchange, seeking legal advice to ensure compliance with national regulations, preparing SOPs for each type of data covering legal aspects, and including a plan to identify, report, and correct any data breaches. The main outputs include elaboration of SOPs, granting of formal authorizations for each data source, and establishment of a mitigation plan for data breaches. 7. The process revision phase focuses on understanding the successes and failures of the initial seven steps, revising and updating the NHWA mechanism based on past experiences, and gaining political commitment to repeat elements of step 1, including obtaining sustainable funding. Tasks include convening a strategic meeting with the multi-stakeholder working group, evaluating and revising NHWA governance, identifying and inviting potential new members, revising HRH indicators, and defining the budget for the next implementation phase. The main outputs include a revised NHWA implementation and governance framework and a plan for including new indicators and stakeholders. 8. The data compilation and analysis phase aims to define data quality and eligibility criteria and collect data for NHWA through different focal points. Tasks include producing a quality assessment of data sources, adopting standards on data quality, flow, periodicity, and use, gathering and aggregating data from multi-stakeholder working group focal points, defining potential new data sources and surveys, designing an extraction strategy to cover gaps in the next implementation round, and preparing a cost/value evaluation for gathering new data. The main outputs include a process document (including legal requirements), a final list of data with quality information, and centralized indicator statistics. 9. The validation phase seeks to obtain validation of NHWA data analyses, the dissemination plan, and documents from the multi-stakeholder working group. Tasks include collecting feedback and guidance on HRH data from a national workshop, drafting a document synthesizing and translating the data for a non-specialized audience, convening a formal executive meeting to validate results and adopt interpretations, preparing a final report, and developing key messages targeting decision-makers in each sector and a broader audience. The main outputs include formalized political and technical validation of the NHWA process and preparation of key messages for decision-makers and the public. 10. The dissemination phase focuses on raising awareness of HRH by disseminating data and documents on NHWA. Tasks include defining target audiences, preparing a communication plan, supporting the diffusion of messages in various media, monitoring messages on HRH, gathering feedback, preparing a report for the multi-stakeholder working group, preparing scientific publications on NHWA findings, and releasing disaggregated data in the public domain if authorized. The main outputs include setting up a system to track dissemination of HRH data messages and releasing a series of communication products with follow-up.
